title: Trading Bot with Claude
author: Cutting-Edge28
selftext:
I've built an algorithmic trading bot with Claude. I haven't tested it with real money yet—it's on a demo account. And I think it's generated good profits. I haven't become a millionaire, nor do I expect to, but I think it can work for making a little money and turning a profit.    
It has a Telegram bot that sends notifications for every trade it opens or closes. It runs 24/7, scanning the market every 30 seconds, connected to an Oracle VPS, and trades during New York and London market hours. It works with just 7 instruments, reads real-time news and breaking headlines, uses the macroeconomic calendar, and has take-profit and stop-loss protection. Here are some screenshots of Friday’s trades. I welcome any suggestions or feedback.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nice build, and the Telegram alerts and the circuit breaker are good touches. In the screenshots most trades are small wins, with one oil loss that is larger than several of them, so I'd look at the average win against the average loss over a few weeks, not one day. Demo accounts also tend to fill cleanly, so the real spread and slippage on oil and gold could cut those small wins a lot. I'd track the results against a plain baseline and keep the rules frozen while you collect enough trades. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to test a rule with fees and slippage included.

comments.author: chunky_doorstep
comments.body: The Oracle VPS and Telegram notifications sound like a thoughtful setup, but Friday's demo trades aren't enough to know how the bot handles a rough market. I'd track execution slippage, disconnected sessions and how its news filter responds to sudden headlines. I'm on Moon for manual market wagers myself and I'd want an automated system to prove it can avoid bad situations before putting real money behind it.

replies.author: QATSAlgo
replies.body: Start with one instrument and one explicit setup: when to enter, position size, stop, exit, and a stop-for-the-day. Keep those rules fixed while testing with costs, then paper trade and log fills before considering real money. Disclosure: we are QATS. If you prefer visual logic to coding, our optional paid Bot Builder lets you inspect entry/exit blocks and backtest: [https://prop.qats.us/bot-builder](https://prop.qats.us/bot-builder) . It is for our crypto/TradFi perpetuals environment; evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated. Are you trying to automate an existing setup or still define the strategy?

comments.author: Successful-Mud-2000
comments.body:
Cool project, I built a bot too so I know how much work goes into this. After going through all your screenshots the setup looks solid, daily circuit breaker, ATR trailing and a max risk per trade is more than most people do. A few things I noticed:



Possible bug 1: in the closed position message for ticket 709558909 the close price shows 95.942, which is the entry price. The TP was 96.804 and the P&L is +25.86, so the P&L looks right but the close price being logged is wrong. Worth checking before you trust your stats



Possible bug 2: in the status message EURUSD shows ATR 0.000. Probably just the display rounding to 3 decimals, but if the bot uses that same rounded value for the trailing stop or position size on EURUSD it could break things



Also the close reason says Stop Loss / Take Profit for every trade. I would log which one it actually was, otherwise its hard to know if the trailing stop is helping or not



On the strategy side, most of the profit is oil longs, several at the same entry. With everything going on in the Middle East oil has been trending up, so I would want to see how it does when oil reverses or goes sideways before calling it an edge. Those stacked longs would all hit SL together



And demo fills are perfect. Spread and slippage on real money can eat a lot when some targets are only a few dollars



If you track a few months of profit factor and max drawdown on demo and it still holds, then go live really small. Nice work
